title: Junction — Traffic Signal Lab
description: Design an intersection, time its signals, and watch a real car-following simulation reward or punish you.
concept: A microscopic traffic simulator you can redesign in real time. Pick a layout — four-way cross, T-junction or roundabout — choose signals, an all-way stop or give-way priority, then tune the green splits while vehicles queue, accept gaps and turn across each other. Every car runs an IDM car-following model and yields at geometrically-derived conflict points, so a bad phase plan produces genuine spillback. A hill-climbing optimiser runs ~20 headless simulations to find better splits, and the whole study exports as a CSV engineering report.
features: Three layouts (cross, T-junction, roundabout) built from one data-driven route/conflict engine
Three control modes: fixed-time signals, protected-permissive left phasing, all-way stop, plus roundabout give-way
Live phase editor — per-phase green sliders, amber and all-red clearance, click a phase to jump to it
Per-approach demand sliders, turning-movement mix and four scenario presets (balanced, AM peak, arterial, gridlock)
Hill-climbing split optimiser that runs headless simulations to minimise average delay
HCM-style level-of-service grading, per-approach delay/queue table and a delay-over-time chart
Export a CSV engineering report, save a PNG snapshot, copy a share link, store the best plan in localStorage

interaction.mouse: Drag the green, demand and turning sliders; the map updates live
interaction.click: Tap an approach on the map to raise its arrival rate, tap the junction centre to pause, click a phase card to jump to that phase
interaction.touch: Full touch support — tabs become a bottom sheet and the camera tightens on small screens
interaction.keyboard: space play/pause · 1/2/3 layout · o optimise · e CSV report · r reset
